title: Read the fictional scenario and evidence rules
nav: 1. Read the fictional scenario and evidence rules
objective: Annotate the Scenario Data sheet as fact, estimate or unknown.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: The capstone puts the whole Blueprint method into practice on one realistic case. Before you start, understand what the scenario gives you, what it deliberately leaves out, and how evidence will be judged.
The case is an unnamed, fictional knowledge-work organization with 2,000 employees. It is not a real customer, and no external research is needed.

items: **The COO** is the simulated executive sponsor and wants more support capacity this quarter, without losing quality.
**The CRO** wants more consistent meeting preparation in sales.
**A technical champion** coordinates the platform owners.
**The procurement and signature process** is unknown.

blocks.caption: How to treat scenario inputs
head: Kind
Example from the case
How to use it
rows: 200 potential support users; 240 workdays a year
A training fact, labeled as such
Interview timings, such as eight minutes to find approved guidance
An estimate, not a measured baseline
Connector and permission behavior; procurement dates; the baseline
An open question with an owner and a validation step

blocks.x: Label every figure you use. Any assumption you add yourself must be recorded with an owner and a validation plan. The assessor answers questions using only the scenario's facts and will say "unknown, must validate" for anything the scenario doesn't contain.

blocks.label: Boundary
blocks.x: Don't invent a customer name, a real case study, an approved product capability, or a measured outcome. Real customer stories and internal images are not required, and shouldn't be used.
Every input in the scenario has a status. Use it exactly as labeled.

blocks.title: Three kinds of scenario input
blocks.alt: Three cards naming the kinds of input in the capstone scenario: facts, which you may use as stated; estimates, which you must show as ranges with assumptions; and unknowns, which you must turn into open questions with owners.

items.label: Unknowns
items.detail: Open questions, each with an owner
